issue_context.title: Not all users are being subscribed to the mailing list
issue_context.body:
Currently, we only subscribe users to the ConvertKit mailing if they go through the waitlist.  The waitlist path hits a function that attempts to add the user to our mailing list and stores whether that enrollment was successful or not on the signups table.  Signup rows are not created, or required, for users who are invited in via a link; we don't currently attempt to enroll them either since we don't have a boolean on the users table to mark whether it was successful or not.

Solutions:

1. Kill off the signups table and migrate all columns over to the users table.  At some point, we won't have a waitlist, when we start allowing users to freely download, so I imagine that we will end up killing off the waitlist code and the signups table at some point, so it wouldn't be a waste to do it now.  While I generally don't like the idea of combining multiple tables, in this case, it probably makes sense to keep all information about a user in one place, then just add a `has_access` boolean to make being invited in.  This would mean that the `added_to_mailing_list` boolean would be right on the user table.

2. Enforce that every user row generated has to have an associated signups row generated as well.  From there, ensure that we are trying to add users to the mailing list no matter which way they are brought in.
comments: I vote for option 1 - it has more work upfront, but I think it brings us closer to a future version of Zed where we no longer have a waitlist or signups.  Also, migrating data in the db such, but any mistakes or screwups are more forgivable earlier on.
Scrap the original text, Max corrected me.  The issue of not all users are being subscribed is still true.  Users getting into the alpha via an invite link are not being added to the mailing list.

review_comments: Let's make this field optional w/ serde so that we can roll this out before we deploy the Zed.dev stuff.
Are we good to just use `#[serde(default)]`?  `bool` defaults to `false`, which will be the correct value until the changes to zed.dev land, where the actual api call to ConvertKit happens.
